criteria.criterion: Using only the illustrative curated securities, a browser submission of one valid retirement input set displays deterministic steady and product-owned early-downturn projections, each with ending balance, depletion timing or full-horizon status, and year-by-year results.

The early-downturn scenario keeps the steady allocation and yield, reduces that allocation’s blended annual growth rate by exactly 20 percentage points in year 1 only, and uses the unadjusted steady blended yield and growth rates in years 2 through the selected horizon; the page visibly discloses this as an illustrative deterministic assumption, not a forecast or financial advice.

In an owner-performed Google Chrome click-and-render run using a $1,000,000 portfolio, 30-year horizon, and 3% inflation, both scenario tables, the illustrative/non-advice disclosures, elapsed time of 1 second or less, invalid-input refusal with cleared output, and zero page-console errors are recorded.
Repeated calls with identical valid inputs return identical scenario results; all allocation amounts use supplied curated securities only and sum exactly in integer cents.
Invalid or unsupported scenario input returns an actionable refusal and leaves no previous comparison summary, scenario value, or scenario table visible.

The representative $1,000,000, 30-year, 3% calculation and rendering completes within 1 second in the documented owner Chrome measurement, and calculation work is bounded by horizon years and curated-security count rather than portfolio cents.

Existing steady-projection behavior remains covered by regression tests; this delivery changes no provider refresh, infrastructure, database, dependency, workflow, credential, telemetry, factory artifact, or CI behavior.

Comparable-difficulty record: Project #60 has three planned Stories (#62–#64), matching failed Project #47’s three approved delivery Stories (#49–#51) before corrective Story #58. Both add a pure calculation engine, connect it to the browser, render allocation/projection-derived results, preserve integer-cent and curated-security limits, and require regression plus real Chrome verification. Both exercise $1,000,000, 30 years, and 3% inflation in real Chrome. Project #47’s failed acceptance evidence in comments 5426602811 and 5426620130 records the missing effective realistic response bound and freeze; Project #60 retains comparable scope while adding the explicit one-second and horizon/security-count bound.
